summary: Add exam-style reasoning on oxidation-number and water-reaction trends, and make the bonding explanation more explicit.

improvements.why: The current oxidation-number questions mostly ask for one value; none has difficulty 4 or asks learners to explain the full trend from valence electrons.
improvements.what: Add one structured comparison of highest oxidation numbers and formula ratios from Na to P, including why the sulfur oxides have +4 and +6, and one misconception-based item distinguishing oxidation number from oxygen-atom count. Use the examiner's ratio error in ER 9701 s23 P12 Q18.

improvements.why: These outcomes have many recall items and past MCQs but no difficulty-4 generated task combining water observations with a subsequent excess-NaOH test.
improvements.what: Add a multi-part beaker-table task in which learners predict solid remaining after water and then after excess NaOH for MgO, Al2O3 and SiO2, and justify amphoteric versus insoluble behaviour. Use the error pattern in ER 9701 w22 P13 Q25; keep solution and suspension distinct.

improvements.why: The many chloride MCQs do not require a full written account of products, observations, balanced equations and acidity across the series.
improvements.what: Add structured exam parts comparing dissolution of NaCl with hydrolysis of AlCl3, SiCl4 and PCl5, including likely pH and the balanced SiCl4 and PCl5 equations. Address the examiner-reported errors of calling AlCl3 neutral and giving phosphorus oxide instead of phosphoric acid (ER 9701 w22 P21 Q3; s23 P22 Q2).

improvements.where: note, after ## Key ideas; teach card 9701-9.2.6
improvements.why: The note states the ionic-to-covalent and basic-to-acidic trends but gives little causal explanation, although outcome 9701-9.2.6 explicitly requires bonding and electronegativity.
improvements.what: Add a short stepwise explanation: increasing nuclear charge with similar shielding raises electronegativity; the oxide and chloride bonding becomes more covalent; metal oxides contain basic oxide ions, Al2O3 is amphoteric, and covalent non-metal oxides form acids. Explain how this predicts water reaction and acid-base behaviour, while avoiding a claim that every intermediate compound follows one simple rule.

improvements.why: ER 9701 w22 P22 Q2 reports that candidates often describe NaCl dissolution as NaOH and HCl formation and lose marks for unbalanced equations or wrong state symbols.
improvements.what: Add a compact worked contrast with state symbols: NaCl dissolves as aqueous ions without hydrolysis, whereas covalent SiCl4 hydrolyses to a white SiO2 solid and HCl; explicitly check atom balance and identify the species responsible for acidity.
